sentences.text: Recent molecular studies indicate that Kentisuchus belongs to Gavialoidea, a parent group containing modern gharials, rather than being a true crocodile.
The genus name honors William Buckland, who originally named the species Crocodylus spenceri based on a partial skull found on the Isle of Sheppey.
Charles Mook erected the genus Kentisuchus in 1955 for the species originally described by Richard Owen in 1849.
Fossils of Kentisuchus have been found in England and France dating to the early Eocene, specifically between 56 and 37.71 million years ago during the Ypresian to Bartonian stages.
Research suggests Kentisuchus dispersed from mainland Europe to islands in the Tethysian archipelago rather than migrating from Africa.
